properties: The original scalar constructor and update correspond to all nine Rust fields and both optional gains, on the declared Python scalar domain.
The checked eight-update axis certificate is reused twice for a four-state planar tracker; all four outputs are finite and each absolute arithmetic error is at most 2^-30 (m or m/s).
Validation specifies every error exit. Below/Above decisions agree strictly with the exact horizontal reference; Uncertain implies distance from threshold at most 2^-28 + 2^-29.
domain: Eight ordered (x,y) measurements; each coordinate and initial position is finite in [-10,10] metres.
Initial velocities are finite in [-2,2] m/s; threshold finite in [-20,20] metres.
Numerical application uses dt=1/8 second, g=1/2, h=1/8, default per-update gains.
adaptations: PlanarTracker, validation and threshold classification are application additions around two original scalar FilterPy GHFilter instances; this is not a full covariance Kalman filter.
The reusable raw Rust GHFilter preserves constructors, fields, options and update order. Its full-state correspondence is distinct from the bounded numerical application claim.
